lines.trans: Tilt the smudged card slightly toward the afternoon sun, Rocio: do you see the first letter?
Two spoons of warm M... and then a small round drawing beside the ink blot!
That tiny round fruit with three pointed leaves is not a lemon: it is an orange!

words.gloss: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)
to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)

lines.trans: Wait: warm M plus grated sweet orange peel! Could M stand for wildflower honey?!
Smell the paper right where the card rested for thirty years, my dear.

words.gloss: to smell (oler a = to smell of/like)

lines.trans: Close your eyes and breathe deeply: garden mint, sweet orange peel, and golden honey!
Of course! Warm honey stays soft and glossy without turning sour or hard as a rock!
And a pinch of grated orange peel brightens the berries without making Mateo pucker his face!
Look at the last clean word in the corner: scatter toasted sliced almonds on top.

words.gloss: corner (outer street corner or cake corner)

lines.trans: Two spoons of warm honey, grated orange peel, and toasted almond flakes!
Tin Three is still warm on the oven rack: run and brush it right now, boss!
Do not move from that piano bench, Carmen, the real cake will be out in five minutes!

Two spoons of warm M... and then a small round drawing beside the ink blot!
That tiny round fruit with three pointed leaves is not a lemon: it is an orange!

Of course! Warm honey stays soft and glossy without turning sour or hard as a rock!
And a pinch of grated orange peel brightens the berries without making Mateo pucker his face!

Smell the paper right where the card rested for thirty years, my dear.

Of course! Warm honey stays soft and glossy without turning sour or hard as a rock!
And a pinch of grated orange peel brightens the berries without making Mateo pucker his face!
Look at the last clean word in the corner: scatter toasted sliced almonds on top.

lines.trans: Two spoons of warm honey, grated orange peel, and toasted almond flakes!
Tin Three is still warm on the oven rack: run and brush it right now, boss!
Do not move from that piano bench, Carmen, the real cake will be out in five minutes!
See you soon!

meanings.note: Marks destination, clock time, and animate direct objects (personal a).

examples.text: Vamos a la estación ahora.
examples.trans: We are going to the station now.

examples.text: El desayuno empieza a las ocho.
examples.trans: Breakfast starts at eight o'clock.

meanings.note: Ahora mismo means 'right now'.

examples.text: Voy para allá ahora mismo.
examples.trans: I am heading there right now.

examples.text: Ahora tenemos cuatro mesas libres.
examples.trans: Now we have four free tables.

alegrar.gloss: to make glad; to cheer up

meanings.en: to make glad; to cheer up
meanings.note: Me alegra / nos alegra means 'it makes me/us glad'.

examples.text: Esa noticia nos alegra mucho.
examples.trans: That news makes us very glad.

examples.text: Las flores alegran toda la mesa.
examples.trans: The flowers brighten up the whole table.

meanings.note: Classic Mediterranean baking ingredient in tarts and biscuits.

examples.text: Rocío hornea galletas crujientes de almendra y limón.
examples.trans: Rocio bakes crunchy almond and lemon biscuits.

examples.text: Tostamos las almendras cinco minutos en el horno.
examples.trans: We toast the almonds for five minutes in the oven.

meanings.note: Tener ... años expresses age; hace ... años means '... years ago'.

examples.text: El año está aquí.
examples.trans: The year is here.

examples.text: Vemos los años desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the years from the door.

meanings.note: Means both a wooden bench in a park or square and a financial bank.

examples.text: Nos sentamos en el banco de madera a la sombra.
examples.trans: We sat down on the wooden bench in the shade.

examples.text: La flecha de latón apunta hacia el banco del parque.
examples.trans: The brass arrow points toward the park bench.

meanings.note: General botanical and culinary word for small fleshy berries (bayas rojas = red berries).

examples.text: Tomás lavó dos cestas llenas de bayas rojas maduras.
examples.trans: Tomas washed two baskets full of ripe red berries.

examples.text: Las bayas dulces combinan muy bien con la masa de almendra.
examples.trans: Sweet berries pair very well with the almond batter.

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine.

examples.text: El suelo está limpio y brillante.
examples.trans: The floor is clean and shiny.

examples.text: Tiene unos ojos brillantes.
examples.trans: She has bright eyes.

meanings.note: Core feminine noun for the human or animal face; central to Spanish idioms like 'dar la cara' ('to step up / take responsibility') and 'verle la cara a alguien'.
Colloquially, 'tener cara' or 'qué cara' means to be shameless or brazen. Also feminine singular of the adjective caro ('expensive').

examples.text: Pero le ves la cara, te emociona, te llega.
examples.trans: But you see her face, she moves you, she gets right to you.

examples.text: ¡Qué cara más dura tienes presentándote aquí sin avisar!
examples.trans: What nerve you have showing up here unannounced!

meanings.note: Coger cariño a = to grow fond of; also a warm term of endearment in Spain.

examples.text: El cariño es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The affection is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre el cariño.
examples.trans: We talk about the affection.

cerrar.gloss: to close; to lock; to turn off (a valve)

meanings.en: to close; to lock; to turn off (a valve)
meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> ie: cierro).

examples.text: Cierro la tienda a las ocho.
examples.trans: I close the shop at eight.

examples.text: Anoche cerramos todas las contraventanas.
examples.trans: Last night we closed all the shutters.

meanings.note: Invariable cardinal number.

examples.text: Faltan cinco minutos para las doce.
examples.trans: It is five minutes to twelve.

examples.text: Tenemos cinco mesas en el patio.
examples.trans: We have five tables in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Alto y claro = loud and clear; ¡Claro! / ¡Pues claro! = Of course!

examples.text: El mensaje es alto y claro.
examples.trans: The message is loud and clear.

examples.text: ¡Pues claro que puedes pasar!
examples.trans: Well of course you can come in!

meanings.note: Unaccented como compares or gives a reason (distinct from interrogative cómo).

examples.text: Está fría como el agua del río.
examples.trans: It is as cold as river water.

examples.text: Todo funciona como debe ser.
examples.trans: Everything works just as it should.

meanings.note: Combines with mí/ti to form conmigo ('with me') and contigo ('with you').

examples.text: Tomo café con leche caliente.
examples.trans: I take coffee with hot milk.

examples.text: Habla con calma, por favor.
examples.trans: Speak calmly, please.

meanings.note: Entrar/salir corriendo = to run in / run out.

examples.text: Corro para no perder el tren.
examples.trans: I run so I do not miss the train.

examples.text: Los niños corrieron hacia la fuente.
examples.trans: The children ran toward the fountain.

meanings.note: Table or soup spoon; cucharita is a teaspoon.

examples.text: Pon una cuchara limpia junto a cada cuenco.
examples.trans: Set a clean spoon beside each bowl.

examples.text: Prueba la sopa de lentejas con esta cuchara.
examples.trans: Taste the lentil soup with this spoon.

meanings.note: Links possession, origin, material (de madera), and contents (taza de té).

examples.text: Es una mesa redonda de madera.
examples.trans: It is a round wooden table.

examples.text: Vengo de la estación de tren.
examples.trans: I am coming from the train station.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition de + masculine article el.

examples.text: El bizcocho acaba de salir del horno.
examples.trans: The cake just came out of the oven.

examples.text: Soy vecino del barrio.
examples.trans: I am a neighbour from the quarter.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Descanso media hora después de comer.
examples.trans: I rest half an hour after lunch.

examples.text: Los huéspedes descansaron muy bien.
examples.trans: The guests rested very well.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb; the noun is el dibujo, a drawing.

examples.text: Mi hija dibuja un gato.
examples.trans: My daughter is drawing a cat.

examples.text: ¿Me dibujas el camino al hotel?
examples.trans: Will you sketch me the way to the hotel?

meanings.note: Unaccented in relative clauses; accented dónde in questions.

examples.text: Esta es la plaza donde compramos flores.
examples.trans: This is the square where we buy flowers.

examples.text: Siéntate donde estés más cómodo.
examples.trans: Sit where you feel most comfortable.

meanings.note: Describes gold colour or golden-brown baked crust.

examples.text: Es una pieza dorada.
examples.trans: It is a golden piece.

examples.text: El del papel dorado del estante de arriba. ¿Por qué?
examples.trans: The one in gold paper from the top shelf. Why?

meanings.note: Los dos / las dos means 'both'.

examples.text: Pongo dos tazas azules en la mesa.
examples.trans: I put two blue cups on the table.

examples.text: Compra las dos válvulas por favor.
examples.trans: Buy both valves, please.

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine; los dulces = sweets/pastries.

examples.text: Es una pieza dulce.
examples.trans: It is a sweet piece.

examples.text: ¿Podemos servir mantequilla salada con mermelada dulce de fresa?
examples.trans: Can we serve salted butter with sweet strawberry jam?

meanings.note: Marks how long an action lasted (durante seis años).

examples.text: Vivió aquí durante seis años.
examples.trans: She lived here for six years.

examples.text: No sonó el teléfono durante la cena.
examples.trans: The phone did not ring during dinner.

meanings.note: Hacerse el duro = to act tough.

examples.text: Es una pieza dura.
examples.trans: It is a hard piece.

examples.text: se hacía el duro
examples.trans: acted tough

echar.gloss: to pour; to toss; to miss (echar de menos)

meanings.en: to pour; to toss; to miss (echar de menos)
meanings.note: Echar un vistazo = take a glance; echar de menos = miss someone.

examples.text: Echa un poco más de agua caliente.
examples.trans: Pour a little more hot water.

examples.text: Te he echado mucho de menos.
examples.trans: I have missed you very much.

meanings.note: Definite article; also appears before feminine nouns starting with stressed /a/ (el agua, el asa).

examples.text: El patio tiene mucha luz.
examples.trans: The courtyard has plenty of light.

examples.text: Pásame el libro de reservas.
examples.trans: Pass me the reservation book.

meanings.note: All Spanish letter names are feminine (la eme, una eme mayúscula).

examples.text: En la tarjeta manchada solo se ve una eme grande escrita con tinta.
examples.trans: On the smudged card you can only see a big M written in ink.

examples.text: Los nombres de Mateo y de su madre empiezan por la letra eme.
examples.trans: Mateo's name and his mother's name both start with the letter M.

meanings.note: Expresses location inside or on top of a surface (en la mesa = on the table).

examples.text: Las tazas están en la mesa.
examples.trans: The cups are on the table.

examples.text: Vivimos en Valencia todo el año.
examples.trans: We live in Valencia all year.

meanings.note: Por encima = on top / over the surface.

examples.text: Pon azúcar glas por encima.
examples.trans: Put powdered sugar on top.

examples.text: Hay un cartel encima de la puerta.
examples.trans: There is a sign above the door.

meanings.note: Forms: ese, esa, esos, esas.

examples.text: Pásame ese cuaderno azul.
examples.trans: Pass me that blue notebook.

examples.text: Esa maleta pertenece a un cliente.
examples.trans: That suitcase belongs to a guest.

esperar.gloss: to wait; to wait for; to hope

meanings.en: to wait; to wait for; to hope
meanings.note: Covers both 'wait (for)' and 'hope'.

examples.text: Espere un momento, por favor.
examples.trans: Wait a moment, please.

examples.text: Esperamos que descanse muy bien.
examples.trans: We hope you rest very well.

esquina.gloss: corner (outer street corner or cake corner)

meanings.en: corner (outer street corner or cake corner)
meanings.note: Outer corner where two streets meet, or the crisp corner of a baking tray.

examples.text: La esquina está aquí.
examples.trans: The corner is here.

examples.text: Vemos las esquinas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the corners from the door.

meanings.note: Feminine noun: la flor, las flores.

examples.text: La flor está aquí.
examples.trans: The flower is here.

examples.text: Vemos las flores desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the flowers from the door.

meanings.note: Collective and countable word for edible fruit (fruta fresca, una fruta redonda).

examples.text: Esa fruta redonda del dibujo no es un limón, sino una naranja dulce.
examples.trans: That round fruit in the drawing is not a lemon, but a sweet orange.

examples.text: En el mercado del sábado siempre compramos fruta madura de temporada.
examples.trans: At the Saturday market we always buy ripe seasonal fruit.

meanings.note: Indicates direction of movement or gaze.

examples.text: Camina hacia el puente de piedra.
examples.trans: Walk toward the stone bridge.

examples.text: Sigue mirando hacia la esquina.
examples.trans: Keep looking toward the corner.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta luego! = See you later!; ¡Hasta mañana! = See you tomorrow!

examples.text: Sigue recto hasta el puente.
examples.trans: Walk straight ahead as far as the bridge.

examples.text: Nos quedamos hasta el viernes.
examples.trans: We are staying until Friday.

meanings.note: Means both a tree leaf and a single sheet of paper.

examples.text: La hoja está aquí.
examples.trans: The leaf is here.

examples.text: Vemos las hojas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the leaves from the door.

meanings.note: Respire hondo = take a deep breath.

examples.text: Es una pieza honda.
examples.trans: It is a deep piece.

examples.text: Respire hondo, Ernesto. Todavía nadie ha escrito nada.
examples.trans: Take a deep breath, Ernesto. Nobody has written anything yet.

meanings.note: Del horno = out of the oven.

examples.text: El horno está aquí.
examples.trans: The oven is here.

examples.text: Vemos los hornos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the ovens from the door.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Inclino la jarra para servir el agua.
examples.trans: I tilt the pitcher to pour the water.

examples.text: Inclinó la caja y oyó una llave.
examples.trans: He tilted the box and heard a key.

meanings.note: Plural jardines, without the written accent.

examples.text: Mi madre tiene flores en el jardín.
examples.trans: My mother has flowers in the garden.

examples.text: Los niños juegan en el jardín.
examples.trans: The children play in the garden.

meanings.note: Feminine form of jefe.

examples.text: En la cocina manda siempre nuestra jefa Rocío.
examples.trans: In the kitchen our head chef Rocio is always in charge.

examples.text: La jefa probó el caldo con una cuchara limpia.
examples.trans: The boss tasted the broth with a clean spoon.

meanings.note: Junto a + noun works like a preposition meaning 'beside / next to'.

examples.text: Siéntate junto a la ventana.
examples.trans: Sit next to the window.

examples.text: Trabajamos juntos en la posada.
examples.trans: We work together at the guesthouse.

meanings.note: Justo aquí = right here; justo al lado = right next door.

examples.text: La llave está justo aquí.
examples.trans: The key is right here.

examples.text: La panadería queda justo al lado.
examples.trans: The bakery is right next door.

meanings.note: Definite feminine singular article before nouns; direct-object feminine pronoun before/attached to verbs.

examples.text: La puerta del patio es azul.
examples.trans: The courtyard door is blue.

examples.text: La habitación tiene mucha luz.
examples.trans: The room has plenty of light.

meanings.note: Used with feminine plural nouns and clock hours (las ocho).

examples.text: Las ventanas dan al jardín.
examples.trans: The windows face the garden.

examples.text: Desayunamos a las ocho.
examples.trans: We have breakfast at eight.

meanings.note: Tu letra means 'your handwriting'.

examples.text: La letra está aquí.
examples.trans: The handwriting is here.

examples.text: Vemos las letras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the handwritings from the door.

meanings.note: Opposite of sucio (dirty).

examples.text: Es una pieza limpia.
examples.trans: It is a clean piece.

examples.text: Aquí tiene un paño limpio y agua fría, Ernesto.
examples.trans: Here is a clean cloth and cold water, Ernesto.

meanings.note: Plural limones.

examples.text: El limón está aquí.
examples.trans: The lemon is here.

examples.text: Vemos los limones desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the lemons from the door.

meanings.note: Los viernes means 'every Friday / on Fridays'.

examples.text: Los vecinos vienen a desayunar.
examples.trans: The neighbours come for breakfast.

examples.text: Daba clases de piano los viernes.
examples.trans: She taught piano lessons on Fridays.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta luego! is Spain's most common everyday farewell.

examples.text: Cruza el puente y luego gira.
examples.trans: Cross the bridge and then turn.

examples.text: ¡Hasta luego, que tengas buen día!
examples.trans: See you later, have a good day!

meanings.note: In cooking, almendra en láminas means sliced/flaked almonds; in art, una lámina is an illustrated plate or print.

examples.text: Rocío echó almendra tostada en láminas por encima del glaseado de miel.
examples.trans: Rocio scattered toasted sliced almonds over the honey glaze.

examples.text: El libro antiguo de botánica tiene láminas pintadas a mano.
examples.trans: The old botany book has hand-painted plates.

meanings.note: Everyday noun related to manchar ('to stain').

examples.text: Esa mancha fresca de pintura sale con agua templada.
examples.trans: That fresh smudge of paint comes out with warm water.

examples.text: Revisa que los manteles blancos no tengan ninguna mancha.
examples.trans: Check that the white tablecloths do not have a single stain.

manchar.gloss: to stain; to smudge; to spot

meanings.en: to stain; to smudge; to spot
meanings.note: Regular -ar verb; the past participle manchado/manchada means 'stained' or 'smudged'.

examples.text: Alguien manchó la esquina de la tarjeta con una gota de tinta azul.
examples.trans: Someone stained the corner of the card with a drop of blue ink.

examples.text: Ponte el delantal blanco para no mancharte la camisa con las bayas.
examples.trans: Put on the white apron so you do not stain your shirt with the berries.

meanings.note: Té de menta = mint tea.

examples.text: La menta es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The mint is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre la menta.
examples.trans: We talk about the mint.

meanings.note: Feminine noun: la miel.

examples.text: La miel es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The honey is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre la miel.
examples.trans: We talk about the honey.

meanings.note: En cinco minutos = in five minutes.

examples.text: El minuto está aquí.
examples.trans: The minute is here.

examples.text: Vemos los minutos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the minutes from the door.

mirar.gloss: to look; to look at; to watch

meanings.en: to look; to look at; to watch
meanings.note: Needs no preposition for 'at' (mira el reloj = look at the clock).

examples.text: Mira qué sol hace esta mañana.
examples.trans: Look how sunny it is this morning.

examples.text: Miramos el mapa antes de salir.
examples.trans: We look at the map before going out.

meanings.note: Agrees with the noun it describes.
In ahora mismo, meaning right now, mismo strengthens the time word ahora. Now comes from ahora; mismo supplies emphasis without agreeing with a person in this expression.

examples.text: Tenemos el mismo trabajo.
examples.trans: We have the same job.

examples.text: Ahora mismo estoy ocupada.
examples.trans: I am busy right now.

meanings.note: In baking, el molde is a cake tin or baking pan; letra de molde means block/printed letters.

examples.text: Repartimos la masa de almendra en tres moldes redondos pequeños.
examples.trans: We divided the almond batter across three small round baking tins.

examples.text: Unta el molde con un poco de mantequilla antes de meterlo al horno.
examples.trans: Grease the baking tin with a little butter before putting it in the oven.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: muevo).

examples.text: Movemos la mesa bajo la sombra.
examples.trans: We move the table into the shade.

examples.text: El viento suave movió las hojas.
examples.trans: The gentle breeze stirred the leaves.

meanings.note: Accented más means 'more / most'; de más = extra.

examples.text: ¿Quiere un poco más de té?
examples.trans: Would you like a little more tea?

examples.text: Es la habitación más tranquila.
examples.trans: It is the quietest room.

meanings.note: Zumo de naranja = orange juice.

examples.text: La naranja está aquí.
examples.trans: The orange is here.

examples.text: Vemos las naranjas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the oranges from the door.

meanings.note: Ni... ni... = neither... nor...; ni una gota = not a single drop.

examples.text: No cae ni una sola gota.
examples.trans: Not a single drop is falling.

examples.text: No tengo ni papel ni bolígrafo.
examples.trans: I have neither paper nor pen.

meanings.note: Placed directly before the verb (or object pronouns) to negate a sentence.

examples.text: Hoy no llueve en Valencia.
examples.trans: Today it is not raining in Valencia.

examples.text: No se preocupe por la hora.
examples.trans: Do not worry about the time.

meanings.note: Plural los ojos.

examples.text: El ojo está aquí.
examples.trans: The eye is here.

examples.text: Vemos los ojos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the eyes from the door.

oler.gloss: to smell (oler a = to smell of/like)

meanings.en: to smell (oler a = to smell of/like)
meanings.note: Irregular boot stem hue- (huelo, hueles, huele, huelen).

examples.text: La cocina huele a canela caliente.
examples.trans: The kitchen smells like warm cinnamon.

examples.text: El jardín huele a flores frescas.
examples.trans: The garden smells of fresh flowers.

meanings.note: Ni una palabra = not a word.

examples.text: La palabra está aquí.
examples.trans: The word is here.

examples.text: Vemos las palabras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the words from the door.

meanings.note: Plural los papeles.

examples.text: El papel está aquí.
examples.trans: The paper is here.

examples.text: Vemos los papeles desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the papers from the door.

meanings.note: Hermano pequeño = younger brother; de pequeño = as a child.

examples.text: Es una pieza pequeña.
examples.trans: It is a small piece.

examples.text: Hay una pequeña tarjeta de cartón atada al asa.
examples.trans: There is a small cardboard card tied to the handle.

meanings.note: Tocar el piano = to play the piano.

examples.text: Por las tardes alguien toca una melodía suave en el viejo piano del salón.
examples.trans: In the afternoons someone plays a gentle melody on the old parlor piano.

examples.text: Hace veinticinco años daba clases de piano muy cerca de esta calle.
examples.trans: Twenty-five years ago I gave piano lessons very close to this street.

meanings.note: De piedra = made of stone.

examples.text: La piedra está aquí.
examples.trans: The stone is here.

examples.text: Vemos las piedras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the stones from the door.

meanings.note: Plural las pieles; covers fruit peel (la piel del limón), human skin, and leather.

examples.text: La piel amarilla de este limón huele de maravilla.
examples.trans: The yellow peel of this lemon smells wonderful.

examples.text: Mateo guarda sus herramientas en una bolsa de piel.
examples.trans: Mateo keeps his tools in a leather bag.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: En primavera pintamos la puerta azul.
examples.trans: In spring we paint the blue door.

examples.text: El abuelo pintó una llave dorada.
examples.trans: Grandfather painted a golden key.

meanings.note: Una pizca de sal is the standard cooking measure for a tiny pinch.

examples.text: Añade una pizca de sal fina a la masa dulce.
examples.trans: Add a pinch of fine salt to the sweet pastry.

examples.text: Probamos una pizca de crema con una cuchara limpia.
examples.trans: We taste a tiny dab of cream with a clean spoon.

meanings.note: Un poco de mantequilla = a little butter.

examples.text: ¿Quiere un poco de miel en el té?
examples.trans: Would you like a little honey in your tea?

examples.text: Quedan pocos minutos para el mediodía.
examples.trans: Few minutes remain until noon.

por.gloss: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)

meanings.en: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)
meanings.note: Por la mañana = in the morning; por favor = please; gracias por = thanks for.

examples.text: Paseamos por el casco antiguo.
examples.trans: We stroll through the old quarter.

examples.text: Por la mañana entra mucho sol.
examples.trans: In the morning plenty of sun comes in.

meanings.note: Shortens to primer before masculine singular nouns (el primer día); also used as adverb ('first').

examples.text: Hoy es mi primer día de trabajo.
examples.trans: Today is my first day of work.

examples.text: La primera habitación está libre.
examples.trans: The first room is vacant.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta pronto! = See you soon!

examples.text: ¡Hasta pronto y buen viaje!
examples.trans: See you soon and safe travels!

examples.text: Esta mañana me desperté muy pronto.
examples.trans: This morning I woke up very early.

meanings.note: Describes the points of a star or compass rose (una estrella de ocho puntas) or the tip of a pencil or knife.

examples.text: La rosa de los vientos tiene ocho puntas dibujadas a tinta.
examples.trans: The compass rose has eight points drawn in ink.

examples.text: Afiló la punta del lápiz antes de empezar a dibujar.
examples.trans: He sharpened the tip of the pencil before starting to draw.

meanings.note: Core connector and relative pronoun (unaccented, distinct from interrogative qué).

examples.text: Espero que descanses muy bien.
examples.trans: I hope that you rest very well.

examples.text: El pan de esta panadería huele genial.
examples.trans: The bread that The baker bakes smells great.

quedar.gloss: to remain / be left; to suit; to meet up (Spain); to stay (quedarse)

meanings.en: to remain / be left; to suit; to meet up (Spain); to stay (quedarse)
meanings.note: Versatile verb: quedan dos ('two left'), le queda bien ('suits you'), quedar al mediodía ('meet at noon'), quedarse ('stay').

examples.text: Solo quedan dos habitaciones libres.
examples.trans: Only two vacant rooms are left.

examples.text: Esa chaqueta te queda muy bien.
examples.trans: That jacket suits you very well.

rallar.gloss: to grate (lemon or orange peel, cheese, bread)

meanings.en: to grate (lemon or orange peel, cheese, bread)
meanings.note: Regular -ar verb;piel rallada de naranja means 'grated orange peel / zest'.

examples.text: Rocío añadió una pizca de piel rallada de naranja dulce al glaseado.
examples.trans: Rocio added a pinch of grated sweet orange peel to the glaze.

examples.text: ¿Puedes rallar la piel de dos limones amarillos sin llegar a lo blanco?
examples.trans: Can you grate the zest of two yellow lemons without reaching the white pith?

meanings.note: Una mesa redonda = a round table.

examples.text: Es una pieza redonda.
examples.trans: It is a round piece.

examples.text: ¿Dónde cuelgo este espejo redondo? ¿A la izquierda de la ventana o a la derecha?
examples.trans: Where do I hang this round mirror? Left of the window or right?

meanings.note: Wire rack for cooling baked cakes.

examples.text: La rejilla está aquí.
examples.trans: The cooling rack is here.

examples.text: Vemos las rejillas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the cooling racks from the door.

meanings.note: Respire hondo = breathe deeply.

examples.text: Salgo al jardín a respirar aire fresco.
examples.trans: I step into the garden to breathe fresh air.

examples.text: Respiró hondo antes de tocar el timbre.
examples.trans: He took a deep breath before ringing the bell.

salir.gloss: to go out; to come out; to leave

meanings.en: to go out; to come out; to leave
meanings.note: Irregular 1st sg salgo; salir corriendo = run out.

examples.text: El pan acaba de salir del horno.
examples.trans: The bread just came out of the oven.

examples.text: Salgo temprano hacia la estación.
examples.trans: I leave early for the station.

seguir.gloss: to continue; to keep (doing); to go straight (seguir recto)

meanings.en: to continue; to keep (doing); to go straight (seguir recto)
meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> i: sigo, sigue, siguió); seguir + gerund = keep doing.

examples.text: Sigue todo recto hasta el puente.
examples.trans: Walk straight ahead to the bridge.

examples.text: ¿El agua sigue caliente?
examples.trans: Is the water still hot?

ser.gloss: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)

meanings.en: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)
meanings.note: Used for names, professions, ownership (es mía), materials (es de madera), and clock time.

examples.text: Soy arquitecta y vivo en Valencia.
examples.trans: I am an architect and live in Valencia.

examples.text: Esa maleta azul es mía.
examples.trans: That blue suitcase is mine.

meanings.note: Followed by bare nouns (sin azúcar, sin sal) or infinitives (sin abrir = unopened).

examples.text: Tomo el té sin azúcar, gracias.
examples.trans: I take my tea without sugar, thank you.

examples.text: Salió de casa sin abrigo.
examples.trans: He left home without a coat.

meanings.note: Hace sol = it is sunny.

examples.text: El sol es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The sun is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre el sol.
examples.trans: We talk about the sun.

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine.

examples.text: Es una pieza suave.
examples.trans: It is a soft piece.

examples.text: Y mire: esta chaqueta de lana suave está limpia y nueva. Pruébela.
examples.trans: And look: this soft wool cardigan is clean and unworn. Try it on.

meanings.note: Por la tarde = in the afternoon; ¡Buenas tardes! = Good afternoon!; llegar tarde = arrive late.

examples.text: ¡Buenas tardes! ¿Tienen una habitación libre?
examples.trans: Good afternoon! Do you have a room free?

examples.text: Perdón por llegar un poco tarde.
examples.trans: Sorry for arriving a little late.

meanings.note: Pagar con tarjeta = pay by card.

examples.text: La tarjeta está aquí.
examples.trans: The card is here.

examples.text: Vemos las tarjetas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the cards from the door.

meanings.note: Usual word in Spain for a sweet tart or birthday cake.

examples.text: Hay tarta de chocolate para el postre.
examples.trans: There is chocolate cake for dessert.

examples.text: Mi abuela hace una tarta de manzana riquísima.
examples.trans: My grandmother makes a delicious apple tart.

meanings.note: Object/reflexive pronoun corresponding to tú.

examples.text: Te guardo un rollo de canela.
examples.trans: I am saving a cinnamon roll for you.

examples.text: ¿Cómo te llamas?
examples.trans: What is your name?

meanings.note: Describes a gentle, pleasant warmth (pan tibio, agua tibia), similar to templado.

examples.text: El pan recién salido del horno todavía está tibio y tierno.
examples.trans: The bread fresh from the oven is still warm and soft.

examples.text: Disuelve la levadura en medio vaso de agua tibia.
examples.trans: Dissolve the yeast in half a glass of lukewarm water.

meanings.note: Con tinta permanente = in permanent ink.

examples.text: La tinta es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The ink is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre la tinta.
examples.trans: We talk about the ink.

torcer.gloss: to twist; to lean; to bend (torcerse = go crooked)

meanings.en: to twist; to lean; to bend (torcerse = go crooked)
meanings.note: Stem-changing o -> ue (tuerzo, tuerce) and c -> z before o/a.

examples.text: Si el pasador está flojo, la pieza se tuerce.
examples.trans: If the pin is loose, the part leans sideways.

examples.text: No tuerzas la llave antigua dentro de la cerradura.
examples.trans: Do not twist the old key inside the lock.

meanings.note: A classic Spanish breakfast is una tostada con tomate.

examples.text: Para desayunar quiero una tostada con tomate.
examples.trans: For breakfast I want toast with tomato.

examples.text: Las tostadas están en la mesa.
examples.trans: The toast is on the table.

meanings.note: Treinta y cinco = thirty-five.

examples.text: Nos dan treinta días de plazo.
examples.trans: They give us thirty days' notice.

examples.text: Son las nueve y treinta y cinco.
examples.trans: It is nine thirty-five.

meanings.note: Invariable cardinal number.

examples.text: Ponemos tres mesas bajo el árbol.
examples.trans: We set three tables under the tree.

examples.text: Empieza con tres frases cortas.
examples.trans: Start with three short sentences.

meanings.note: Forms: un (m sg), una (f sg), unos (m pl 'some/about'), unas (f pl).

examples.text: Quiero un café caliente, por favor.
examples.trans: I would like a hot coffee, please.

examples.text: Hay una mesa libre en el patio.
examples.trans: There is a free table in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Irregular: veo, vi, visto.

examples.text: Desde aquí veo el puente de piedra.
examples.trans: From here I see the stone bridge.

examples.text: ¡Nos vemos luego en el patio!
examples.trans: See you later in the courtyard!

meanings.note: La verdad = honestly / the truth.

examples.text: La verdad está aquí.
examples.trans: The truth is here.

examples.text: Vemos las verdades desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the truths from the door.

volver.gloss: to return; to come back; to do again (volver a + inf)

meanings.en: to return; to come back; to do again (volver a + inf)
meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: vuelvo), past participle vuelto; volverse + adj = become.

examples.text: Vuelvo en cinco minutos.
examples.trans: I will be back in five minutes.

examples.text: Volvió a sonreír enseguida.
examples.trans: He smiled again right away.

meanings.note: Changes to e before words starting with /i/ sound (i- or hi-).

examples.text: Servimos café caliente y pan fresco.
examples.trans: We serve hot coffee and fresh bread.

examples.text: Son las siete y cuarto.
examples.trans: It is quarter past seven.

meanings.note: Standard word for the sharp, tart taste of lemons or unripe fruit.

examples.text: El primer molde lleva un glaseado de zumo ácido de limón.
examples.trans: The first tin has a tart lemon-juice glaze.

examples.text: La miel tibia se mantiene suave sin volverse ácida en el horno.
examples.trans: Warm honey stays smooth without turning sour in the oven.

meanings.note: Carries a written accent on ú.

examples.text: Es una pieza última.
examples.trans: It is a last piece.

examples.text: Diez, once, doce. Exacto hasta la última moneda. ¡Gracias!
examples.trans: Ten, eleven, twelve. Exact to the last coin. Thank you!
